newsitem.title: USA: Fingerhut to 'meet or beat' '97 EPS view.
newsitem.headline: Fingerhut to 'meet or beat' '97 EPS view.

text.p: Fingerhut Cos Inc Chairman Theodore Deikel said Tuesday that he expects the company will "meet or beat Wall Street's expectations" for 1997 earnings of $1.26 a share.
Speaking at the annual meeting, Deikel added that management is also "comfortable" with the Wall Street consensus of $0.16 to $0.17 a share for the second quarter.
In 1996, Fingerhut earned $1.12 a share. For the year-ago second quarter it earned $0.04 a share.

Looking ahead, Deikel told shareholders that the company will focus on new uses for its extensive database of customers. Fine tuning of its database will allow Fingerhut to send out fewer catalogs, with an expected 4.6 million in 1997 compared with 5.0 million in 1996, but have higher sales, he added.
Fingerhut is a database marketing company selling a broad range of products and services.
Using technology such as the Internet, Fingerhut plans to expand globally this year. Deikel said his company plans to sell goods in the United Kingdom through the Internet by the end of 1997.
Deikel also said Fingerhut plans to expand its efforts in the credit business through its Metris Cos financial services subsidiary.
The company is aiming to grow its credit card customer base from approximately 1.8 million now to more than 2.0 million, he added.
